課程綱要.開課單位: 亞際文化研究國際碩士學位學程
課程綱要.課程目標: This course introduces students to the historical formations of inter-Asia cultural studies as movements, thoughts, problematics, and praxis to foreground the trajectories of inter-Asia processes. This entails our investigation of disciplinary demarcations cohered in colonial-imperial-national divides out of which cultural studies emerge, while also critically challenging the boundaries of knowledge production and social practices. Implicated in the process, we will also explore how inter-Asia comes forward and reorients our problematics about imperialism, cold wars, and decolonization long overshadowed by the Anglo-American axis. Drawing on trans-local critical thought-resources in and as a global making process, we will also explore inter-Asia methods with which to problematize “Asia,” to inquire into “inter-Asia subjectivity,” and to experiment with creative and critical space for the emergence of renewed social and cultural movements.

課程綱要.課程名稱(英文): Seminar on the Everyday Cold War
課程綱要.課程目標: The Cold War was not only a geopolitical confrontation between superpowers but also a lived reality that shaped everyday life across the globe. This course examines how the Cold War influenced structures of feeling, cultural expression, political discourse, and social interactions. With a particular emphasis on East and Southeast Asia, and with comparative references to global contexts, we will adopt an interdisciplinary approach to analyze how ideological struggles unfolded in media, education, popular culture, domestic life, and social movements, and how ordinary people navigated the complexities of life under Cold War conditions. By extending beyond conventional diplomatic and military narratives, this course highlights the intimate, localized, and transnational manifestations of the Cold War. Students will develop a critical understanding of how Cold War legacies continue to reverberate in the present.

課程綱要.課程目標: Abstract: This seminar will examine colonialism as historical phenomenon and cultural problem but more importantly as interrelated issues. It is necessary thus to distinguish the study of colonial societies from postcolonial theory, which is an important discourse that has recently impacted and problematized cultural studies. Coloniality as historical phenomenon and cultural mindset constitutes the framework for redefining the cultural nature of coloniality, ultimately as geopolitical process. What is the role of the state and the nature of cultural critique? The last third of the course will focus on case studies. [* indicates required reading; + indicates other recommended reading]

課程綱要.課程名稱(英文): War and Media: History, Technology, Culture
課程綱要.課程目標: 媒介技術與戰爭⾏為是現代性感官經驗的⼀體兩⾯。從電影、攝影、電報、廣播、繪畫、⽂學，以⾄於網路遊戲，媒介不僅再現了戰爭，更扮演實際動員與宣傳戰爭的基礎設施。本課程從台灣、東亞、到世界等不同歷史時空，探討「戰爭-媒介」此⼀⽂化技術綜合體對敘事模式與美學形式的若⼲影響及擾動，並試圖探問在戰爭動員之外，媒介使⽤者或創作者的⾃由可能。 本課程以⽂獻閱讀討論為主，搭配參訪活動（新竹帝國海軍第六燃料場、⿊蝙蝠中隊⽂物館等、新竹科學園區探索館）與電影放映。歡迎對電影與媒介研究、戰爭軍事史、批判理論有興趣之同學選修。

課程綱要.課程名稱(英文): Women‘s Cinema and New Media: From Gaze to Play
課程綱要.課程目標: Identify key figures and movements in the history of women’s cinema. Analyze films and media texts from a feminist perspective, considering the role of gender, genre, and cultural context. Evaluate the impact of women filmmakers and media creators in world cinema and media culture. Engage with critical theories and debates surrounding women and film/media in diverse perspectives. Develop research and presentation skills through class discussion, assignments and a final research project, which may take the form of a written paper, creative media work, or essay film.

課程綱要.評量配分比重: Attendance and Class Participation: 15+15% ・Up to 2 absences with reasons will be accepted. 1.5 points will be deducted starting from the third absence (even with reason). ・participation of the 2 guest lectures and 1 film festival week group discussion is mendatory. (3 points will be deducted for missing any of the events) ・Interaction in class is required. Extra scores (15%) can be earned by participation in class. Extra points might be added for more participation in class discussion. Students should keep notes of your own participation. Online Participation: 15% - All students must complete at least 2 required reading materials each week. Students will be divided into group A and B. Group A post questions or ideas for share according to the weekly reading/ screening 2 days prior to meeting in class. Group B must reply to one of Group A student’s post to have a discussion 1 day prior to our meeting in class. A and B will rotate each week. 1.5 points will be deducted each week if the student does no post anything in time. Key discussions: 15% - Each student should prepare a 5-10 min of review/ analysis/thoughts on events/ screenings of WMW film festival for group discussion. Pop-up quiz: 20% - 5 Pop-up quizzes will be given on related topic of the week. It will be open book. (Example: Please list 1 film that can be considered “body genre” according to Linda Williams’ definition and explain why.) Presentation of Final Project: 15% -Each student will give a 5-10 min presentation of their research proposal (research topic and methodology) of the final research project. Final Project: 20% ・Each student must complete a final project—a research paper (10-15 double-spaced pages, Chicago style), or media work/ documentary/ essay film (under 15 min) that reflects on the theories we’ve learned—by the end of the semester. Pay attention to the required academic style and use citation correctly to avoid plagiarism. ・Lateness: 24hrs after deadline, 5 points will be deducted. 48 hrs after deadline, 10 points will be deducted. After 72 hrs, the final project gets 0 point.
